title: Read the Updated Role Catalog
subtitle: A governed change from the feedback loop
scenario: The role profile catalog changed since the last hire: a handheld scanner was added to the Logistics Coordinator profile after a prior onboarding's feedback showed the role needed it. Read the updated, versioned catalog and understand how a governed change - not an ad-hoc grant - improves it.
input: Role Profile: Logistics Coordinator (Operations), version 1.1.0. Accounts: identity, email, directory. Software: Logistics Suite, Email/Calendar. Hardware: Standard laptop, handheld scanner (added v1.1.0 from onboarding feedback). Access groups: ops-general, warehouse-readonly. Pay class: Non-exempt / Hourly. Change owned and ratified by the People Ops Lead.
instructions: Read the updated profile and note what changed and why.
Answer the four questions about governed change, versioning, and least-privilege.
Validate to mint the updated role profile record.

questions.prompt: Why was the handheld scanner added to the profile?

options.text: A prior hire requested it ad hoc on their first day
Onboarding feedback showed the role needed it, and People Ops ratified the change
The IT Provisioner added it without review

questions.explain: The loop works as designed: profile-feedback proposed it, and the People Ops Lead ratified it into a new version. Governed change, not an ad-hoc grant.

questions.prompt: What does the version bump to 1.1.0 tell you?

options.text: The catalog change is tracked and auditable over time

questions.explain: Versioning makes the change auditable: you can see what the role got, when, and who approved it - the same discipline as any governed reference.

questions.prompt: Does adding the scanner break least-privilege?

options.text: No - it is now part of the role profile, so it is still granted by role
Yes - any new item is over-provisioning
Only if the hire asks for it

questions.explain: Least-privilege is about granting by role, not by request. Because the scanner is now in the profile, every Logistics Coordinator gets it consistently and auditably.

questions.prompt: Who ratifies a change to the catalog?

options.text: The People Ops Lead, who owns the catalog

questions.explain: Feedback proposes; the People Ops Lead ratifies. Ownership of the change never leaves the catalog owner.

copilotPrompt: Explain a governed change to a role profile catalog: why a handheld scanner was added (from onboarding feedback), what a version bump signifies, why it still respects least-privilege, and who ratifies the change.
successMessage: Updated profile read. The catalog improved through the loop - governed, versioned, and still least-privilege.

intro.heading: Before you plan: the catalog learned

sections.title: The loop closed
sections.body: The scanner is not new noise - it is last quarter's feedback ratified into the profile. What one hire needed became what every hire in the role now gets, by design.

sections.title: Change is versioned
sections.body: A governed catalog records its changes. Version 1.1.0 means the addition is tracked and auditable, not a silent edit someone made and forgot.

sections.title: Still least-privilege
sections.body: Adding to the profile does not break least-privilege - it extends the role's defined set. Access is still by role, and the scanner is now part of that role for everyone.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: An updated role profile record the plan expands - now including the scanner the loop taught the catalog to grant.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd update the role checklist once People Ops approved the addition, then use the new version for every hire in that role.

bestFit.how: a Dataverse entitlements table with an owner in People Ops, edited through a form
a database read keyed on role, returning the entitlement list the plan expands

takeaway.heading: Updated profile read
points: You saw a governed change: the scanner added from onboarding feedback.
The version bump makes the change tracked and auditable.
Adding to the profile keeps least-privilege - access is still by role.
The People Ops Lead ratified it; ownership stayed with the catalog owner.
The workflow can now provision the improved role from a versioned catalog.
